idiom_name: #[derive(FromRow)] struct + impl PersonRow { async fn find/update } over sqlx::query_as
implementation_notes: The row is a struct deriving sqlx::FromRow (or using query_as with a tuple), and the gateway methods live in an impl block that takes &Pool or &mut PgConnection: an async fn find returning Option<Self>, and insert/update/delete methods executing query statements. sqlx supplies mapping and compile-time-checked SQL, but the row carries no persistence state and owns no connection, so the structure - struct plus associated functions - is hand-written. This is the default for async services; choose it when the SQL must stay visible and the runtime is tokio or async-std.
pitfalls: The query! macros need DATABASE_URL at build time or a checked-in .sqlx offline cache; a CI without either fails to compile.
Every database call returns Result: ignoring it is a must_use warning and a silently skipped write.
A row struct must not hold a connection or transaction guard - borrow/lifetime and Send bounds make that a design dead end; pass the executor per call.

variants.name: diesel table DSL with insert_into/update/find
variants.implementation_notes: diesel's generated schema module gives the table a typed handle: people::table.find(id).first::<PersonRow>(conn) for the find, diesel::insert_into(people).values(&new_person) for the insert, and diesel::update(people::table.find(id)).set(people::deps.eq(3)) for the update. The statements are built declaratively and checked at compile time; the row type stays a plain struct with Queryable/Insertable/AsChangeset derives, so the per-row object is still assembled by the developer - which is why this is a library-assisted manual realization rather than a row-owned gateway.
variants.idiom_name: diesel::insert_into / update / table.find over derived Queryable/Insertable structs
pitfalls: find() only exists for single-column primary keys; composite-key tables need explicit filters.
The schema module is generated by diesel_cli and must be regenerated (or the build fails with confusing type errors) after migrations.
Connections are not Sync; a gateway function taking &mut SqliteConnection cannot be shared across threads without a pool.
